text: And after all the weather was ideal, for they could not have had a more perfect day for a garden party if they had ordered it. <break time="0.8s" /> The air was windless and warm, the sky was without a cloud, and the gardener had been up since dawn, mowing the lawns and sweeping them until they seemed to shine. <break time="0.8s" /> Before breakfast was even over, the men came to put up the marquee, and Missus Sheridan, who wanted the children to arrange everything themselves, told them to treat her as an honored guest. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura, who was considered the artistic one in the family, ran out to meet the four workmen, still holding a piece of bread and butter in her hand. <break time="0.8s" /> She tried to sound businesslike by copying her mothers voice, but it sounded so affected that she felt ashamed and stammered like a little girl instead. <break time="0.8s" /> When she suggested the lily lawn, the tall, lanky, freckled workman looked around and said that a marquee there would not be conspicuous enough. <break time="0.8s" /> In the end he chose a place against the karaka trees, and Laura was sorry, because the trees, with their broad gleaming leaves and clusters of yellow fruit, would be hidden. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the tall workman pinched a sprig of lavender and smelled it, and Laura, deeply charmed, wondered how many of the men she knew would ever have done such a thing. <break time="0.8s" /> It was all the fault of these absurd class distinctions, she decided, and to show how much at home she felt, she took a big bite of her bread and butter.
